title: Whisperr automatic-event catalogue and conformance cases

commonProperties.description: Flat properties every automatic event carries when the runtime can supply them. No value, no key.

reserved.description: The reserved automatic event names. The server accepts each one for every app without registration.

placeholder.description: A value the harness cannot control. Expected events carry this token, and the harness substitutes its SDK's own value.

automatic.description: always: the SDK sends it on its own. framework: automatic only where the framework makes it cheap, otherwise a manual API. manual: the app calls an SDK method.

countsAsActivity.description: true when the event means the user did something in the app. The server counts only these as user activity.

device.description: What the harness makes the platform report. A missing key means the runtime cannot supply that value. platform, os_name, sdk_name and sdk_version are fixed by the SDK under test and appear as placeholders instead.

storage.description: empty (default): a fresh install. legacy_sdk_state: storage holds state an older SDK wrote (a stored user, no stored app version).

launch.description: The process starts with this app version installed, the harness builds the client on the case storage, identifies user_1, and the app comes to the foreground (a cold start).

background.description: The harness clock moves forward afterMs, then the app goes to the background.

foreground.description: The harness clock moves forward afterMs, then the app comes back to the foreground in the same process (a warm start).

terminate.description: The process ends with no further lifecycle signal. Storage survives.

screen.description: The app calls the SDK's manual screen API with this name.

pushOpened.description: The user opens a notification with this data payload, and the app hands it to the SDK's push-open API.

pushPermission.description: The app reports this notification permission through the SDK's permission API.

optOut.description: The app calls the SDK's opt-out API.

optIn.description: The app calls the SDK's opt-in API.

expected_event.description: An event as serialized, minus identity fields, occurred_at, and context (context must still carry $message_id, as wire.json pins).
